extracted.intended_audience: ERC panel members and external peer reviewers evaluating Starting, Consolidator, and Advanced grants
extracted.subtask_description: Operational evaluation guide for ERC panel members and external reviewers applying the single statutory criterion of scientific excellence when assessing research proposals (Starting, Consolidator, Advanced). Describes how to assess the research project and PI, the two-stage procedure, score definitions, and explicit reviewer rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Excellence (single statutory criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: By EU regulation, the ERC may use ONLY one criterion: scientific excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This single criterion is operationalized as evaluations of two objects: (A) the Research Project and (B) the Principal Investigator. Apply ONLY the scientific excellence criterion — no policy, equity, regional, or strategic considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Ground‑breaking nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Goes beyond state-of-the-art; addresses important problems or barriers; tackles new and emerging fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the proposal is ground‑breaking and advances the frontier of knowledge. Look for work that opens new directions rather than incremental advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance for advancing knowledge and wider scientific or societal impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate both intellectual significance for the field and potential wider impacts; consider how important the outcomes would be if successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Scientific approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundness of objectives; appropriateness of methodology; existence of testable hypotheses where applicable; quality of preliminary work; feasibility within timeframe; risk and risk‑management appropriate to ambitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess methodological rigor, clarity of objectives, feasibility given resources and time, and whether risk is identified and appropriately managed. Risk and ambition are considered positive features when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — Intellectual capacity and creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Track record demonstrating exceptional capacity; original contributions to the field; intellectual leadership beyond the immediate group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence of high intellectual independence, originality, and leadership in publications, outputs, or prior achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — Commitment to the project
rubrics_metrics.description: PI's time commitment and independence: time commitment thresholds (≥50% for Starting/Consolidator, ≥30% for Advanced); independence from previous mentors (for Starting/Consolidator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm stated percentage of time devoted to the project and evaluate whether that commitment is realistic and sufficient to deliver the proposed work. For early career PIs, consider demonstrable independence from former supervisors/mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator — Career‑stage‑appropriate excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of excellence appropriate to career stage: Starting Grant (2–7 years post‑PhD; 'exceptional promise'), Consolidator (7–12 years; 'outstanding research achievements'), Advanced (any stage; 'exceptional leader' with 'ground‑breaking achievements').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the PI's achievements relative to expected norms for their declared career stage; do not apply a one‑size‑fits‑all standard across career stages or fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑Stage Evaluation Process — Stage 1 Panel‑Only review
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel review of extended synopsis + CV. Panel members give individual scores on the ERC scale (A / B / C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 1 identifies top proposals for external review based on the synopsis and CV. Score each proposal on its own merits; do not apply quotas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑Stage Evaluation Process — Stage 2 External expert review
rubrics_metrics.description: Top-ranked Stage 1 proposals receive 3–5 external expert reviews; panel re-evaluation incorporates external reviews; interview with the PI is mandatory for Starting/Consolidator finalists; final A/B/C scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External reviews provide in‑depth assessment of the full proposal. Panels must integrate external advice, re-evaluate, and conduct interviews where required before making final recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score Definitions — A (Outstanding)
rubrics_metrics.description: A — Outstanding: ground‑breaking, exceptional PI, fully convincing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for proposals that convincingly meet the excellence threshold at the highest level and should be recommended for funding if budget allows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score Definitions — B (Excellent but with weaknesses)
rubrics_metrics.description: B — Excellent but with some weaknesses: high quality but not at A level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for very strong proposals that contain identifiable weaknesses or uncertainties that prevent assignment of the top rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score Definitions — C (Below ERC threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: C — Does not fully meet ERC criteria / below excellence bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for proposals that fail to meet the ERC's excellence standard for funding; substantial deficiencies in project and/or PI evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer rule — Apply only scientific excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply ONLY the scientific excellence criterion — no policy, equity, regional, or strategic considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude non‑scientific factors (e.g., policy alignment, regional balance, institutional considerations) from assessment and scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer rule — Score proposals on their own merits (no quotas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Score each proposal on its own merits — no quotas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not artificially adjust scores to satisfy distributional quotas or panel targets; each proposal should be judged independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer rule — Risk and ambition as positives
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk and ambition are positive features, not negative ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High‑risk, high‑gain proposals should not be penalised for risk per se; evaluate whether risk is justified by potential impact and whether it is appropriately managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer rule — Contextual assessment of PI CV
rubrics_metrics.description: PI's CV must be assessed in the context of career stage and field norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret publication record, outputs, and achievements relative to discipline practices and the PI's declared career stage; account for atypical career paths where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer rule — Interdisciplinary proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals from interdisciplinary work should be assessed by all relevant disciplines on the panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure interdisciplinary proposals receive expertise across the relevant fields; panels should involve members who can judge each disciplinary component.
